text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key habit is following naming conventions: choose clear, descriptive names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes your code simpler to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you return to a project months later, well-organized code saves you time and prevents mistakes. In short, writing clean code is an investment that pays off every day.
